mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility has risen consistently from -28.6% to -19.6% over four weeks, signaling gradual return-to-office behavior. This sustained upward trend in commuting activity will drive weekday retail visits and foot traffic, producing net positive RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 9 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses direction and falls below -22% in any of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has declined from 9.6% to 6.9% over four weeks, indicating reduced time spent at home. This behavioral shift reflects increased willingness to leave residential spaces for discretionary activities, directly driving higher retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 2.7 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 8.5% in the next week, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below its prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Transit station mobility remains severely depressed at -45.6%, indicating sustained suppression of public transportation use. When TRANSIT falls below -45%, retail mobility remains constrained because transit-dependent populations cannot easily access retail destinations, keeping RETAIL_REC negative over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -45% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -45.6% in most recent week
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -40% within the next two weeks and RETAIL_REC subsequently increases above its prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility has declined sharply from -9.4% to -18.0% over four weeks, signaling reduced outdoor leisure activity. This contraction in parks visits indicates a behavioral regime shift away from discretionary outdoor activities, which will suppress retail-and-recreation mobility as consumers reduce overall out-of-home discretionary behavior over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 8 percentage points below the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined 8.6 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS rebounds above -12% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery and pharmacy mobility has remained stable and elevated at 7.3–7.4% across four weeks, indicating sustained essential shopping behavior. When essential-goods mobility is stable and positive while retail-recreation is negative, consumers are substituting discretionary retail for essential purchases. This substitution pattern will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks unless discretionary confidence recovers.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 7% while RETAIL_REC remains below -10%
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stable at 7.3–7.4% while RETAIL_REC at -10.7%
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 5% or RETAIL_REC rises above -8% within two weeks, indicating a shift in consumer substitution patterns.

This dual suppression will keep RETAIL_REC negative over the next four weeks unless both proxies recover simultaneously.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES below -20% AND TRANSIT below -45% in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:Both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain severely depressed in t-0w
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES rises above -15% or TRANSIT rises above -40% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its prior 28-day mean.

This regime transition from home-centric to office-centric activity will accelerate retail-recreation recovery as workers resume commute-adjacent shopping, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks.
